title: Maxwell Logan establishes Woodbridge Printery
text: On January 1, 1918, Maxwell Logan acquired printing equipment and moved it to Green Street in Woodbridge. He later published the Woodbridge Leader and Woodbridge Independent.

title: Edwin Paul Beckerman begins work as library director
text: On January 1, 1964, Edwin Paul Beckerman began work as the first director of Woodbridge Township's new public library system.

title: Woodbridge marks New Jersey's 300th anniversary
text: On January 1, 1964, Woodbridge held a New Jersey Tercentenary ceremony at Town Hall, including a flag raising and the swearing-in of the Council under a new form of government.

title: Woodbridge begins its 300th anniversary celebration
text: On January 1, 1969, Woodbridge Township began its 300th anniversary celebration with a flag raising and a reception hosted by the mayor.

title: Morse and Vail demonstrate the telegraph in Morristown
text: On January 6, 1838, Samuel Morse and Alfred Vail publicly demonstrated their telegraph at the Speedwell Ironworks in Morristown, New Jersey.

title: Woodbridge School No. 1 is dedicated
text: On January 6, 1877, Woodbridge School No. 1 was dedicated. The historic school later became an important landmark in the township.

title: Edison laboratory films a sneeze
text: On January 7, 1894, Thomas Edison's West Orange laboratory filmed Fred Ott sneezing. The short film was later registered as the first motion picture copyrighted in the United States.
source: Thomas Edison Papers / Library of Congress research

title: Woodbridge's Captain Carlsen is rescued
text: On January 10, 1952, Woodbridge resident Captain Kurt Carlsen was rescued after remaining aboard the stricken Flying Enterprise until the final moments. His courage made international headlines.

title: Alice Paul is born in Mount Laurel
text: On January 11, 1885, women's suffrage leader Alice Paul was born in Mount Laurel, New Jersey.
source: Alice Paul Institute / New Jersey historical research

title: George Washington Bridge receives its official name
text: On January 13, 1931, the Port Authority announced that the new Hudson River bridge would be named the George Washington Bridge. It opened later that year.

title: Absecon Lighthouse is first lit
text: On January 15, 1857, Absecon Lighthouse in Atlantic City was first lit, helping guide ships along the New Jersey coast.

title: Final section of the New Jersey Turnpike opens
text: On January 15, 1952, the final northern section of the New Jersey Turnpike opened, completing the 118-mile highway.

title: Woodrow Wilson becomes New Jersey governor
text: On January 17, 1911, Woodrow Wilson was inaugurated as New Jersey's governor. He later became the 28th president of the United States.

title: Christine Todd Whitman becomes New Jersey governor
text: On January 18, 1994, Christine Todd Whitman was inaugurated as New Jersey's 50th governor and the first woman to hold the office.

title: Electric lighting system begins operating in Roselle
text: On January 19, 1883, Thomas Edison's electric lighting system began operating in Roselle, demonstrating community-wide electric lighting.
source: Thomas Edison Papers / New Jersey historical research

title: Plans begin for Woodbridge School No. 1
text: On January 21, 1876, Woodbridge school trustee William H. Berry recommended buying land for a two-story, six-room school designed for 800 students, with a proposed budget of $25,000.

title: Alfred E. Driscoll becomes New Jersey governor
text: On January 21, 1947, Alfred E. Driscoll was inaugurated as governor of New Jersey.

title: Edison's Black Maria studio is completed
text: On February 1, 1893, construction was completed on Thomas Edison's Black Maria motion-picture studio in West Orange.

title: The Broker train derails in Woodbridge Township
text: On February 6, 1951, the Pennsylvania Railroad train known as The Broker derailed in Woodbridge Township. The incident prompted a major investigation into rail safety.
source: Interstate Commerce Commission investigation; Woodbridge historic-tour research

title: The Stone Pony opens in Asbury Park
text: On February 8, 1974, the Stone Pony opened in Asbury Park, becoming one of New Jersey's best-known live-music venues.

title: Joe Pesci is born in Newark
text: On February 9, 1943, actor Joe Pesci was born in Newark, New Jersey.

title: Construction begins on the S.S. Woodbridge Victory
text: On February 10, 1945, the keel was laid for the S.S. Woodbridge Victory, a World War II cargo ship named in honor of Woodbridge Township.
source: Woodbridge Township Historical Association; shipbuilding records

title: Edison Memorial Tower is dedicated
text: On February 11, 1938, the Thomas Edison Memorial Tower was dedicated at the Menlo Park site in what is now Edison, New Jersey.

title: New Jersey National Guard is officially desegregated
text: On February 12, 1948, New Jersey's National Guard was officially desegregated by General Order No. 4, making the state an early leader in integrating its military forces.
source: New Jersey Department of Military Affairs

title: First liver transplant in New Jersey is performed
text: On February 14, 1989, the first liver transplant in New Jersey was performed at University Hospital, formerly part of UMDNJ-New Jersey Medical School, in Newark.
source: University Hospital / New Jersey medical-history research

title: Dr. Fred H. Albee dies
text: On February 15, 1945, Woodbridge Township resident Dr. Fred H. Albee, a pioneer in orthopedic surgery, died. During World War I he directed a U.S. military hospital in Colonia.

title: Woodbridge Township is incorporated
text: On February 21, 1798, Woodbridge Township was incorporated under New Jersey's Township Act of 1798.

title: Abraham Lincoln visits Trenton
text: On February 21, 1861, President-elect Abraham Lincoln visited Trenton and addressed the New Jersey Legislature while traveling to his inauguration.
source: New Jersey State Archives / Lincoln historical research

title: Iselin Volunteer Fire Company No. 1 is incorporated
text: On February 22, 1922, Iselin Volunteer Fire Company No. 1 was incorporated in Woodbridge Township. Its charter included 20 members, and Frank Gallagher was its first fire chief.

title: Woodrow Wilson is inaugurated as U.S. president
text: On March 4, 1913, former New Jersey Governor and Princeton University president Woodrow Wilson was inaugurated as the 28th president of the United States.

title: Raritan Township is formed
text: On March 17, 1870, Raritan Township was formed from portions of Woodbridge and Piscataway. It was renamed Edison in 1954.
source: Genealogical Society of New Jersey, Middlesex County locality guide

title: Woodbridge organizes a civilian Home Defense League
text: On March 21, 1917, Woodbridge Township organized a civilian Home Defense League as the United States prepared to enter World War I.

title: S.S. Woodbridge Victory is completed and christened
text: On March 29, 1945, the S.S. Woodbridge Victory was completed and christened. The World War II cargo ship was named in honor of Woodbridge Township.
source: Woodbridge Township Historical Association; shipbuilding records

title: Thomas Mundy Peterson votes in Perth Amboy
text: On March 31, 1870, Thomas Mundy Peterson of Perth Amboy became the first African American in the United States to vote under the Fifteenth Amendment.

title: Roy Plunkett discovers Teflon in New Jersey
text: On April 6, 1938, chemist Roy Plunkett discovered Teflon while working at DuPont's Jackson Laboratory in New Jersey.

title: Paul Robeson is born in Princeton
text: On April 9, 1898, singer, actor and civil-rights advocate Paul Robeson was born in Princeton, New Jersey.

title: Roosevelt Borough is formed from Woodbridge territory
text: On April 11, 1906, Roosevelt Borough was formed from part of Woodbridge Township. The borough was later renamed Carteret.

title: Middlesex Water Company is incorporated
text: On April 17, 1896, Middlesex Water Company was incorporated. The company sought permission to install water pipes beneath Woodbridge's public streets.

title: Jackie Robinson makes his professional debut in New Jersey
text: On April 18, 1946, Jackie Robinson made his professional baseball debut with the Montreal Royals against the Jersey City Giants at Roosevelt Stadium.
source: National Baseball Hall of Fame / New Jersey baseball history

title: Rahway Township is formed
text: On April 19, 1858, Rahway Township was formed from territory that had previously been part of Woodbridge Township.

title: George Washington enters Trenton
text: On April 21, 1789, President-elect George Washington entered Trenton beneath a triumphal arch while traveling to New York for his first inauguration.

title: George Washington stays at Woodbridge's Cross Keys Tavern
text: On April 22, 1789, President-elect George Washington stayed overnight at Woodbridge's Cross Keys Tavern while traveling to New York for his first inauguration.
source: New Jersey historic marker; Woodbridge historical marker

title: S.S. Woodbridge Victory is delivered
text: On April 24, 1945, the S.S. Woodbridge Victory was delivered at the Bethlehem-Fairfield Shipyard in Baltimore. The World War II cargo ship was named in honor of Woodbridge Township.
source: Shipbuilding records; Woodbridge Township historical research

title: Woodbridge proposes a larger high school
text: On April 29, 1949, Woodbridge school officials proposed a larger high school to serve the township's growing student population. Woodbridge Senior High School opened in September 1956.

title: Edison tests an experimental electric railway
text: On May 13, 1880, Thomas Edison tested an experimental electric railway at Menlo Park, New Jersey.

title: New Jersey Constitutional Convention begins
text: On May 14, 1844, New Jersey's Constitutional Convention began in Trenton to consider changes to the state's governing document.

title: Woodbridge Volunteer Fire Company No. 1 dedicates its firehouse
text: On May 18, 1969, Woodbridge Volunteer Fire Company No. 1 dedicated its new firehouse.

title: Edison demonstrates the Kinetoscope
text: On May 20, 1891, Thomas Edison demonstrated the Kinetoscope at his West Orange laboratory to the Federation of Women's Clubs.
source: Thomas Edison Papers / motion-picture history research

title: Woodbridge and Piscataway settlement agreement is signed
text: On May 21, 1666, representatives of Woodbridge and Piscataway signed a settlement agreement with Governor Philip Carteret, setting terms for settlement and land allotment.

title: Woodbridge Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument is dedicated
text: On May 30, 1916, Woodbridge dedicated its Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument at Main Street and Rahway Avenue.

title: Woodbridge receives its official charter
text: On June 1, 1669, Woodbridge received its official charter from King Charles II, formally establishing the township.

title: First drive-in movie theater opens in New Jersey
text: On June 6, 1933, the first drive-in movie theater opened in Pennsauken, New Jersey.

title: Woodbridge dedicates its first official Town Hall
text: On June 14, 1924, Woodbridge Township celebrated its 255th anniversary and dedicated its first official Town Hall as a memorial to local residents who served in World War I. About 30,000 people attended the celebration and parade.

title: Atlantic City's Steel Pier opens
text: On June 18, 1898, Atlantic City's Steel Pier opened with a celebration featuring sharpshooter Annie Oakley.

title: Atlantic City's first Boardwalk opens
text: On June 26, 1870, Atlantic City's first Boardwalk opened along the beachfront.

title: New Jersey adopts its first state constitution
text: On July 2, 1776, New Jersey adopted its first state constitution, declaring independence from Great Britain. The constitution remained in effect for 68 years.

title: Woodbridge physician publicly declares freedom for 14 people
text: On July 4, 1783, Woodbridge physician Dr. Moses Bloomfield publicly declared the freedom of 14 people he had enslaved at a gathering on his farm. The event is remembered as an early milestone in the movement against slavery in America.

title: Larry Doby becomes the American League's first Black player
text: On July 5, 1947, Paterson-raised Larry Doby became the first African American player in the American League.
source: New Jersey official history; Baseball Hall of Fame

title: Crowds gather for Woodbridge Speedway's opening event
text: On July 6, 1928, about 15,000 racing fans gathered at the new Woodbridge Speedway, a wooden board track that became known as one of the world's fastest half-mile raceways.

title: Edison conceives the phonograph at Menlo Park
text: On July 18, 1877, Thomas Edison conceived the phonograph at his Menlo Park laboratory in New Jersey.
source: Thomas Edison Papers / National Park Service

title: Jersey Joe Walcott wins the heavyweight championship
text: On July 18, 1951, Jersey Joe Walcott defeated Ezzard Charles to become world heavyweight boxing champion. At age 37, he was the oldest heavyweight champion at that time.

title: U.S. Lighthouse Service is established
text: On August 7, 1789, the federal Lighthouse Service was established. New Jersey's Sandy Hook Lighthouse later became part of the nation's lighthouse system.

title: Atlantic City names its beachfront walkway the Boardwalk
text: On August 17, 1896, Atlantic City formally gave its beachfront walkway the name “The Boardwalk.”

title: Victor Talking Machine Company begins making Victrolas in Camden
text: On August 22, 1906, the Victor Talking Machine Company began manufacturing Victrolas in Camden, New Jersey.

title: Abraham Browning helps popularize the Garden State nickname
text: On August 24, 1876, Camden attorney Abraham Browning spoke on New Jersey Day at the Centennial Exhibition in Philadelphia. He is traditionally credited with helping popularize New Jersey's nickname, the Garden State.

title: Amelia Earhart lands at Newark Airport
text: On August 25, 1932, Amelia Earhart landed at Newark Airport after completing the first nonstop transcontinental flight by a woman.

title: The Beatles make their first New Jersey appearance
text: On August 30, 1964, the Beatles performed their first New Jersey concert at Atlantic City Convention Hall.

title: Edison receives a patent for a motion-picture camera
text: On August 31, 1897, Thomas Edison received a patent for his kinetographic motion-picture camera.

title: Atlantic City hosts its first Inter-City Beauty Contest
text: On September 7, 1921, Atlantic City hosted its first Inter-City Beauty Contest. The event helped launch the tradition that became the Miss America Pageant.
source: Miss America / Atlantic City historical research

title: Three new Woodbridge schools open
text: On September 9, 1964, three new Woodbridge schools opened: JFK Memorial High School, Avenel Junior High, and School No. 27 in Colonia.

title: Barron Library opens in Woodbridge
text: On September 11, 1877, Barron Library opened in Woodbridge as the first free public library in Middlesex County. The building later became the Barron Arts Center.

title: Bon Jovi releases the New Jersey album
text: On September 19, 1988, Bon Jovi released its fourth studio album, New Jersey.

title: Bruce Springsteen is born in Long Branch
text: On September 23, 1949, musician Bruce Springsteen was born in Long Branch, New Jersey.

title: Marconi demonstrates wireless telegraphy at Twin Lights
text: On September 30, 1899, Guglielmo Marconi demonstrated wireless telegraphy at Twin Lights in Highlands, transmitting messages from a ship and receiving them at the lighthouse.

title: Edison Lamp Works begins commercial production
text: On October 1, 1880, Edison Lamp Works began commercial production of incandescent lamps at Menlo Park, New Jersey.

title: Martin Luther King Jr. speaks at Monmouth College
text: On October 6, 1966, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. spoke at Monmouth College in West Long Branch, New Jersey.

title: Toni Morrison receives the Nobel Prize in Literature
text: On October 7, 1993, Princeton professor Toni Morrison was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

title: New Jersey Devils earn their first victory
text: On October 8, 1982, the New Jersey Devils recorded their first victory, defeating the New York Rangers 3–2 at the Meadowlands.
source: NHL / New Jersey Devils historical records

title: Giants Stadium opens
text: On October 10, 1976, Giants Stadium opened in East Rutherford, with the New York Giants hosting the Dallas Cowboys in the first regular-season game.

title: Albert Einstein arrives in Princeton
text: On October 17, 1933, Albert Einstein arrived in Princeton to begin work at the Institute for Advanced Study.

title: Thomas Edison dies in West Orange
text: On October 18, 1931, Thomas Edison died at his home in West Orange, New Jersey.
source: National Park Service / Thomas Edison National Historical Park

title: George Washington Bridge is dedicated
text: On October 24, 1931, the George Washington Bridge was dedicated. It opened to traffic the following day.

title: Woodbridge Hook and Ladder Company No. 1 holds its organizing meeting
text: On October 28, 1897, members held the organizing meeting for Woodbridge Hook and Ladder Company No. 1.

title: Woodbridge Fire Company meets in its new firehouse
text: On October 29, 1901, Woodbridge Fire Company No. 1 held its first meeting in its new School Street firehouse.

title: Woodbridge Fire Company No. 1 adopts its name and bylaws
text: On November 4, 1897, Woodbridge's volunteer fire company adopted the name Woodbridge Hook and Ladder Company No. 1 and approved its bylaws.

title: New Jersey Turnpike opens its first southern section
text: On November 5, 1951, the first southern section of the New Jersey Turnpike opened to traffic.

title: Rutgers and Princeton play the first intercollegiate football game
text: On November 6, 1869, Rutgers defeated Princeton 6–4 in New Brunswick in what is recognized as the first intercollegiate football game in the United States.

title: Queen's College charter is signed in New Brunswick
text: On November 10, 1766, the charter for Queen's College, later Rutgers University, was signed in New Brunswick by Royal Governor William Franklin.

title: Woodbridge adopts its official township seal
text: On November 11, 1885, Woodbridge Township's Town Committee adopted the design for the official township seal, featuring symbols of its clay, ceramics and maritime industries.

title: Holland Tunnel opens
text: On November 13, 1927, the Holland Tunnel opened, connecting New Jersey and New York beneath the Hudson River.

title: Apollo 12 launches with Princeton alumnus Pete Conrad in command
text: On November 14, 1969, Apollo 12 launched with Princeton alumnus Charles “Pete” Conrad Jr. serving as commander.

title: New Jersey becomes the first state to ratify the Bill of Rights
text: On November 20, 1789, New Jersey became the first state to ratify the amendments that became the Bill of Rights.
source: U.S. Senate / New Jersey State Archives

title: USS New Jersey returns to active service
text: On November 21, 1950, the battleship USS New Jersey returned to active service during the Korean War.

title: Washington's army passes through Woodbridge
text: On November 28–29, 1776, George Washington and the Continental Army passed through Woodbridge during their retreat toward New Brunswick.

title: William Livingston is born
text: On November 30, 1723, William Livingston was born in Albany, New York. He later became New Jersey's first governor.

title: New Jersey Turnpike section opens from Bordentown to Woodbridge
text: On November 30, 1951, a 40-mile section of the New Jersey Turnpike opened between Bordentown and Woodbridge.

title: First issue of the New-Jersey Gazette is published
text: On December 5, 1777, the first issue of the New-Jersey Gazette was published in Burlington by Isaac Collins. It became New Jersey's first continuously published newspaper.
source: New Jersey State Library / American Antiquarian Society

title: Edison demonstrates the phonograph
text: On December 7, 1877, Thomas Edison demonstrated his phonograph at the offices of Scientific American in New York. The invention had been developed in New Jersey.

title: USS New Jersey is launched
text: On December 7, 1942, the battleship USS New Jersey was launched at the Philadelphia Navy Yard, with New Jersey Governor Charles Edison and his wife Carolyn attending.
source: U.S. Navy / New Jersey historical research

title: Frank Sinatra is born in Hoboken
text: On December 12, 1915, singer and actor Frank Sinatra was born in Hoboken, New Jersey.

title: Port Authority Bus Terminal opens
text: On December 15, 1950, the Port Authority Bus Terminal opened in Manhattan, serving commuters traveling between New Jersey and New York.

title: First New Jersey Lottery ticket is sold
text: On December 16, 1970, Governor William T. Cahill purchased the first New Jersey Lottery ticket.

title: New Jersey ratifies the U.S. Constitution
text: On December 18, 1787, New Jersey became the third state to ratify the U.S. Constitution. The state convention in Trenton approved it unanimously.

title: First indoor collegiate football game is played in Atlantic City
text: On December 19, 1964, the Liberty Bowl was played indoors at Atlantic City's Convention Hall. Utah defeated West Virginia 32–6.

title: First Lincoln Tunnel tube opens
text: On December 22, 1937, the first tube of the Lincoln Tunnel opened to traffic between New Jersey and Manhattan.

title: Bell Labs demonstrates the transistor
text: On December 23, 1947, scientists at Bell Labs in New Jersey demonstrated the transistor, a breakthrough that helped transform electronics.

title: Washington leads the Delaware River crossing
text: On December 25, 1776, George Washington led Continental Army troops across the Delaware River from Pennsylvania into New Jersey in preparation for the attack at Trenton.

title: Washington's forces win the Battle of Trenton
text: On December 26, 1776, George Washington's troops surprised Hessian forces in Trenton and won an important American victory during the Revolutionary War.

title: Woodbridge Free School Fund trustees hold their final meeting
text: On December 27, 1920, Woodbridge's all-male Free School Fund trustee board held its final meeting, marking the transition to an all-women board elected earlier that fall.

title: USS New Jersey is recommissioned
text: On December 28, 1982, the battleship USS New Jersey was recommissioned for service.

title: Edison demonstrates electric lighting at Menlo Park
text: On December 31, 1879, Thomas Edison publicly demonstrated incandescent electric lighting at Menlo Park, illuminating about 100 lamps.
